case_results.question: Explain the attention mechanism in simple language.

attempt_results.question: Explain the attention mechanism in simple language.
attempt_results.answer: Attention lets a model look at different parts of a sequence and give each part a weight when building a representation. In self‑attention, every token can “pay attention” to all other tokens in the same sequence. This simple idea has helped tasks such as reading comprehension and abstractive summarization.

attempt_results.question: Give one example that helps explain the main concept.
attempt_results.answer: One example is the sinusoidal positional encoding: each token’s position is represented by a sinusoid whose wavelength ranges from \(2\pi\) to \(10000\cdot2\pi\). This gives every position a unique, smoothly varying representation that the model can learn to attend to, illustrating how the Transformer encodes positional information without recurrence.

attempt_results.question: Give one example that helps explain the main concept.
attempt_results.answer: One example is the sinusoidal positional encoding: each token’s position is represented by a vector of sine and cosine values whose wavelengths form a geometric progression from \(2\pi\) to \(10000\cdot2\pi\). This lets the model learn relative positions by combining these periodic signals. The result is that the same positional pattern can be extrapolated to longer sequences.

attempt_results.question: Give one example that helps explain the main concept.
attempt_results.answer: One example is the sinusoidal positional encoding: each position i is given a vector whose components are sin(i/10000²ᵏ/d) and cos(i/10000²ᵏ/d), with wavelengths ranging from 2π to 10000·2π. This lets the model learn to attend to different positions by encoding relative distances in a continuous, periodic way.
